method.summary: Each soil's typical properties are compared with the crop's requirements on six factors. The rating is set by the hardest-to-fix factors and nudged down by factors that management can improve.

factors.ph: Share of the soil's typical pH range inside the crop's optimal range (>=40% good; some overlap moderate; only inside absolute limits poor; none severe).
factors.drainage: Soil drainage classes compared with the crop's preferred and tolerated classes.
factors.depth: Soil depth class compared with the crop's minimum depth class.
factors.salinity: Soil salinity/sodicity risk compared with the crop's salinity tolerance.
factors.fertility: Natural soil fertility compared with the crop's fertility demand (manageable with inputs).
factors.texture: Soil texture compared with the crop's preferred textures (manageable). Unclassified soils get no penalty.

rating_rule: Take the lowest level among pH, drainage, depth and salinity: good = highly_suitable, moderate = suitable, poor = marginal, severe = unsuitable.
If that result is highly_suitable but fertility or texture is not good, lower it to suitable.
If it is suitable but fertility or texture is poor, lower it to marginal.
method.score: 0-100 weighted average of factor levels (pH 30, drainage 25, depth 15, salinity 10, fertility 10, texture 10), used only to order soils inside the same rating.
method.overrides: None applied. If field evidence contradicts a rating, add an override here with a reason and a source rather than editing the output.

limitations: Ratings use soil-group typical values, not a farm's measured pH or texture; a soil test overrides them.
Climate (temperature, rainfall, altitude) is not part of this file; compare a location with crops.json climate ranges separately.
Ratings inherit the evidence level of each crop; check evidence_level before presenting as firm advice.
